title: The prairie no longer looks like a plaid from the air
items: Flying over 1835, the open prairie used to read as an even grid of light and dark squares. It now breaks into irregular stands of lush and thin grass, with yellower and fresher patches.
At 50–150 m up, the grass no longer lines up in rows toward the horizon.
Up close, at walking height, the grass looks as it did. The patchiness is a reconstruction, listed under Liberties.
